claims.claim: Eustathius of Antioch was Patriarch of Antioch from 324 to 330.
Eustathius was born at Side in Pamphylia.
Eustathius died in exile at Trajanopolis in Thrace, most probably in 360, according to some already in 336 or 337.
Eustathius was first bishop of Beroea in Syria before becoming patriarch of Antioch.
Eustathius was one of the most prominent opponents of Arianism at the Council of Nicaea in 325.
Eustathius was banished to Trajanopolis in Thrace by order of Emperor Constantine.
A discourse by Eustathius on the words of Proverbs 'The Lord created me in the beginning of his ways' survives in fragmentary form.
In his Proverbs discourse, Eustathius discussed Christ's resurrection and Mary's encounter with the risen Christ.
Eustathius was the first to attempt a Logos-Man Christology against the prevalent Logos-Sarx doctrine.
